judged_text: When the sync-endpoint response lacks refresh_token, the code writes the literal placeholder string "refresh_token" into the parsed data, which callers like office365calendar spread over the stored credential key (o365AuthCredentials = {...o365AuthCredentials, ...tokenResponse.data}), overwriting the real refresh token. The user's real OAuth refresh token is silently destroyed and replaced with a constant; if APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED or CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is later unset, the credential can never be refreshed again and the integration dies with an opaque provider error.

adjudication.rationale: The new helper `parseRefreshTokenResponse` explicitly injects a placeholder refresh token when the parsed response lacks one: `if (!refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token) { refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"; }` (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts). In Office365 token refresh, the returned `.data` is spread into the existing credential object: `o365AuthCredentials = { ...o365AuthCredentials, ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data) };` (packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts). If the sync endpoint / minimum schema path returns no `refresh_token`, this spread will overwrite the real stored `refresh_token` with the constant string, causing silent credential corruption and future refresh failures.
